newsitem.title: USA: US stocks end mixed, rocked by weak Aug durables.
newsitem.headline: US stocks end mixed, rocked by weak Aug durables.

text.p: U.S. stocks rode a mini rollercoaster to a mixed finish, rocked by an unexpectedly weak August durable goods report that left traders scrambling to jettison some economically sensitive issues.

"The durables point to an economic slowdown and fortify the Fed's decision (on Tuesday) not to raise short-term rates. But a slowdown raises the question about future corporate earnings," said Peter Cardillo of Westfalia Investments.
After early selling and late morning buying, the Dow industrials settled down nine to about 5869.
But winners beat losers 13-9 on very heavy NYSE volume of about 499 million shares, swollen by end-of-quarter window-dressing.
The tech-laden Nasdaq Composite rose three to 1228, well off its 1237.26 intraday high.

The long bond rallied 19/32 to yield 6.88 percent. The Commerce Department said orders for big-ticket items fell a surprisingly steep 3.1 percent -- the sharpest drop since April 1995 and following a downwardly revised 1.4 percent rise in July. Separately, the Labor Department said weekly jobless claims jumped by 11,000 to 340,000 for the week ended Sept 21.

A.C. Moore, senior investment strategist at Dunvegan Associates, said that the Dow came under pressure "as the durable goods report showed there won't be the push in earnings for many industrial stocks." Caterpillar lost 1/2 to 74-1/4, Alcoa was off 1/4 to 59 and International Paper lost 1/4 to 41-7/8.

The Dow Jones Transportation Average slumped 1.10 percent to 2049 as investors shed airline stocks on worries over higher fuel costs and slower domestic travel. UAL fell 1-1/8 to 45-1/4, AMR lost 2-1/4 to 79-1/2 and Delta fell 7/8 to 70-1/2.
Defensive stocks like drug, beverage and food issues fared better as they were deemd less vulnerable to economic swings.
Merck rose two to 70-3/4, Coca-Cola added 3/8 to 51-1/2 and Procter & Gamble was up 3/8 to 96-3/8.

Stocks got a late morning boost as word spread that influential Morgan Stanley global strategist Barton Biggs was more bullish on U.S. stocks. Biggs said stocks could rally five to 10 percent in the short-term, citing impressive bond and dollar action after the Fed voted to hold rates steady. "That sent a ripple of enthusiasm to the tape," said Moore.
The final revision to second-quarter Gross Domestic Product is due Friday. A 4.6 percent GDP growth rate is expected after the 4.8 percent reading in the second estimate.
Dow component DuPont rose 1-7/8 to 89 after the company forecast third-quarter net earnings would top estimates by at least 10 percent due to strong results in its upstream petroleum operations.
Among the day's IPOs, retailer Abercrombie & Fitch, which outfitted the expeditions of Teddy Roosevelt and Ernest Hemingway, surged 7-1/8 to 23-1/8.
Xionics Document Technologies sured 2-3/8 to 14-3/8 in its Wall Street debut. Xionics designs technology for linking office printers, computers and the Internet.
Gap Inc slumped 1-1/8 to 29-1/2.
Morgan Stanley cut Gap to outperform from strong buy on the belief the retailer's sales gains will be weaker during the rest of the year than in the spring and summer.

Silicon Graphics lost 1-3/8 to 22-1/4 after forecasting first-quarter profits will fall "materially below" market expectations because of product transitions and microprocessor production problems. Morgan Stanley and Dean Witter downgraded the stock.
Mentor Graphics, which also warned of an earnings shortfall, lost 2-7/8 to 9-1/2. Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs downgraded Mentor Graphics.
Burlington Industries tumbled 2-7/8 to 10-3/8 after forecasting lower quarterly results due to a slowdown in its denim operations.

TSCI extended its losses, off 4-1/2 to 11 after forecasting a third-quarter loss. The First Call consensus was $0.14. Shares of the maker of communications software slumped 5-1/4 Wednesday on earnings worries.

Seitel rose 3-1/2 to 37 after news that third-quarter revenues would be significantly above the year-ago quarter. Seitel develops and markets data, geophysical information used by the oil industry in exploration and devlopment.

Transport Holding soared 18-3/8 to 70-1/8 and Conseco added 2-5/8 to 49-1/8. Conseco agreed to buy the provider of cancer insurance and other supplemental health insurance products for $70 a share in Conseco common stock.
The NYSE Composite scored a record closing high, up 0.69 to 365.99.
The Nasdaq Composite rose 3.32 to 1227.98.
The S&P 500 index rose 0.03 to 685.86.
(Figures official as of 1645 EDT/2045 GMT)
